metas.name: Princess Mononoke
metas.description:
Captures an ecological war with no pure side. Iron Town needs the forest cut to survive; the forest gods need the humans gone; a prince cursed by a dying god tries to see with unclouded eyes.

After a deadly curse forces him from home, young warrior Ashitaka journeys west and is drawn into a conflict between ancient forest spirits, an iron town, and a wolf-raised girl.

metas.name: Pan's Labyrinth
metas.description:
Captures a child's fantasy as the only available resistance. Spain, 1944: a girl with a fascist stepfather descends to a faun's tasks while the adult war continues above ground, and fantasy is never 'just' escape.

In 1944 Francoist Spain, an imaginative young girl meets a faun who tells her she's a princess and that she must prove her worthiness by completing three dangerous tasks.

metas.name: Paddington 2
metas.description:
Captures decency as something contagious. A bear framed for stealing the pop-up book he wanted to buy his aunt, sent to prison — and the prison improves because he is in it.

Paddington, now happily settled with the Brown family and a popular member of the local community, picks up a series of odd jobs to buy the perfect present for his Aunt Lucy's 100th birthday, only for the gift to be stolen.

metas.name: Yeelen
metas.description:
Captures a myth from inside its own cosmology. Mali, Bambara legend: a son fleeing his sorcerer father across desert and village, carrying stolen sacred objects, toward a confrontation filmed as light itself.

A young man with magical powers journeys to his uncle to request help in fighting his sorcerer father.

metas.name: Russian Ark
metas.description:
Captures 300 years of history in one held breath. A single unbroken shot drifts through the Hermitage, past czars and ballrooms, with the camera as a ghost nobody quite sees.

A 19th century French aristocrat, notorious for his scathing memoirs about life in Russia, travels through the Russian State Hermitage Museum and encounters historical figures from the last 200+ years.

metas.name: Paprika
metas.description:
Captures dreams invading waking life as a parade. A device that lets therapists enter dreams is stolen, and reality dissolves into a marching band of refrigerators and dolls; Inception's debt is on screen.

When a machine that allows therapists to enter their patients' dreams is stolen, all hell breaks loose. Only a young female therapist, Paprika, can stop it.

metas.name: The Lighthouse
metas.description:
Captures two men rotting in each other's company. A rock in a storm, gaslight, seagull taboos, and two keepers descending into myth, flatulence and murder inside a frame almost square enough to be a trap.

Two lighthouse keepers try to maintain their sanity while living on a remote and mysterious New England island in the 1890s.

metas.name: Valerie and Her Week of Wonders
metas.description:
Captures puberty as a village fairy tale. A thirteen-year-old's coming-of-age rendered as folk-horror dream logic — vampire grandmothers, lecherous priests, possibly magic earrings — where every adult is a monster of one kind or another.

Surreal dream-like tale that combines several themes into one fantastical world.

metas.name: The Saragossa Manuscript
metas.description:
Captures storytelling itself as a folk labyrinth. A Napoleonic officer finds a manuscript and falls into tales within tales within tales — gypsies, kabbalists, ghosts, duels — for three hours in Wojciech Has's nested Polish epic.

Upon finding a book that relates his grandfather's story, an officer ventures through Spain meeting a wide array of characters, most of whom have a story of their own to tell.

metas.name: Häxan
metas.description:
Captures a lecture dissolving into delirium. Christensen's silent Swedish study of witchcraft keeps abandoning its own lecture format for re-enactments — sabbaths, torture chambers, possessed nuns — and from 1922 remains wilder than most folk horror made since.

Fictionalized documentary showing the evolution of witchcraft, from its pagan roots to its confusion with hysteria in Eastern Europe.

metas.name: Kwaidan
metas.description:
Captures folklore as pure painted atmosphere. Kobayashi adapts Lafcadio Hearn's ghost tales on vast studio sets — a snow spirit, a blind biwa player performing for the dead — the closest Japanese equivalent to Parajanov's tableau method.

A collection of four Japanese folk tales with supernatural themes.

metas.name: Uncle Boonmee Who Can Recall His Past Lives
metas.description:
Captures an animist world where the supernatural needs no emphasis. A dying man in the Thai jungle is visited at dinner by his wife's ghost and his son returned as a monkey spirit, and everyone accepts this with total calm.

Dying of kidney disease, a man spends his last, somber days with family, including the ghost of his wife and a forest spirit who used to be his son, on a rural northern Thailand farm.

metas.name: The Holy Mountain
metas.description:
Captures meaning stacked in images until it overloads. Jodorowsky's alchemical procession — a Christ figure and seven archetypes played by industrialists and generals — assembles some of the densest tableaux ever put on film, grotesque and deliberate.

In a corrupt, greed-fueled world, a powerful alchemist leads a messianic character and seven materialistic figures to the Holy Mountain, where they hope to achieve enlightenment.

metas.name: Medea
metas.description:
Captures two cosmologies colliding. Pasolini casts Maria Callas, who barely sings a note, as the barbarian priestess Jason brings home to a rational, modern Corinth with no room for her gods — the archaic ritual world filmed in Cappadocia's stone landscapes.

After his quest to retrieve the fabled Golden Fleece, Jason returns to Greece with powerful sorceress Medea. However, when the king banishes her, it's only human that Medea plots her furious revenge. Can they escape her wrath?

metas.name: Prospero's Books
metas.description:
Captures maximalism as a system. Greenaway adapts The Tempest by layering handwriting, water, calligraphy and early digital compositing over John Gielgud voicing nearly every role — an image-world so dense it becomes a library you wander rather than a plot you follow.

The magician Prospero attempts to stop his daughter's affair with an enemy.

metas.name: The Fall
metas.description:
Captures storytelling as barter. Tarsem spent years shooting a suicidal stuntman's improvised fairy tale to a little girl in a 1920s hospital, across two dozen countries with no green screen; he needs her help, and she keeps changing the story by listening.

In 1920s Los Angeles, a bedridden patient in a hospital captivates a young girl with a fantastic tale of heroes, myths, and villains on a desert island.

metas.name: The Company of Wolves
metas.description:
Captures the folk tale's actual content — appetite, danger, metamorphosis — that the children's versions politely remove. Jordan and Angela Carter nest werewolf tales inside a sleeping girl's dream, all fog, forests and practical-effect transformations.

A teenage girl in a country manor falls asleep while reading a magazine, and has a disturbing dream involving wolves prowling the woods below her bedroom window.

metas.name: Viy
metas.director: Aleksandr Ptushko, Konstantin Ershov, Georgiy Kropachyov
metas.description:
Captures a folk tale told at full demonic strength. A seminarian must pray three nights over a witch's corpse in a village church; Soviet special effects, a Gogol story, and a final night that still startles.

A young priest is ordered to preside over the wake of witch in a small old wooden church of a remote village. This means spending three nights alone with the corpse with only his faith to protect him.

metas.name: Céline and Julie Go Boating
metas.description:
Captures two women hacking a melodrama from the audience seats. A librarian and a magician find a haunted house where the same Victorian drama replays daily; they enter it, swap places with its characters and start stealing the plot with the help of magic sweets.

A mysteriously linked pair of young women find their daily lives preempted by a strange boudoir melodrama that plays itself out in a hallucinatory parallel reality.

metas.name: The Purple Rose of Cairo
metas.description:
Captures a film character noticing he's being watched, and stepping out. A Depression-era waitress goes to the same romance every day until its hero leaves the screen for her — and the other characters, stuck mid-plot, have to improvise without him.

During the Depression in 1935 New Jersey, a lonely waitress with an abusive husband who takes comfort from the movies is stunned when a movie character walks off the screen and into the real world, offering her the hope of a happi...

metas.name: Groundhog Day
metas.description:
Captures a loop that turns out to be a curriculum. It wasn't in your 363, which surprised me too. A weatherman relives one day until the day is no longer the constraint — the rare infinitely-referenced film that is also exactly as good as its reputation.

A curmudgeonly weatherman finds himself stuck in a time loop and is forced to relive the same day over and over again.

metas.name: The Man from Earth
metas.description:
Captures an entire science-fiction epic conducted as a conversation. A professor tells his colleagues he's a 14,000-year-old caveman who stopped ageing; nobody leaves the room, no effect is ever shown, and the argument itself becomes the spectacle.

A professor's impromptu retirement party becomes a mysterious interrogation when he reveals to his colleagues that he has a longer and stranger past than they can imagine.

metas.name: Being John Malkovich
metas.description:
Captures a portal into someone else's head, rented out at $200 a session. A puppeteer finds a door on floor 7½ that drops you behind Malkovich's eyes for fifteen minutes — the transducer problem played as office farce, then as tragedy.

A puppeteer discovers a portal that leads literally into the head of movie star John Malkovich.

metas.name: Mr. Nobody
metas.description:
Captures a life as the full tree of its branches. The last mortal human, aged 117, tells his biography and keeps contradicting himself, because every childhood coin-flip version happened; the film refuses to prune, and the unpruned version is the portrait.

A boy stands on a station platform as a train is about to leave. Should he go with his mother or stay with his father? Infinite possibilities arise from this decision. As long as he doesn't choose, anything is possible.

metas.name: The Science of Sleep
metas.description:
Captures dreams as a handmade TV studio inside a shy man's skull. A Mexican illustrator in Paris can't keep his dream-logic — cardboard cameras, cellophane water, a one-second time machine — from leaking into the courtship he's botching while awake.

A man entranced by his dreams and imagination is love-struck with a French woman and feels he can show her his world.

metas.name: Dave Made a Maze
metas.description:
Captures a living-room fort that is bigger, and lethal, inside. An artist builds a cardboard maze he claims he can't finish or escape; his girlfriend leads a rescue party in with documentary crew in tow. Every trap is cardboard. It kills people anyway.

Dave, an artist who has yet to complete anything significant in his career, builds a fort in his living room out of pure frustration, only to wind up trapped by the fantastical pitfalls, booby traps, and critters of his own creation.

metas.name: Swiss Army Man
metas.description:
Captures a friendship with a corpse who is also a toolkit. A castaway rides a flatulent body to shore and teaches it how to be a person — jet-ski farts, earnest puppet dioramas of ordinary life, and a sincerity that sneaks up on the gross-out premise.

A hopeless man stranded on a deserted island befriends a dead body, and together they go on a surreal journey to get home.

metas.name: Kuroneko
metas.description:
Captures a ghost story staged like Noh theatre in a bamboo grove. A mother and daughter-in-law, murdered by samurai, return as cat-spirits sworn to drink samurai blood — until one victim is their own son and husband. Mist, wire-work leaps, and vengeance colliding with the vow that powers it.

Two women are raped and killed by samurai soldiers. Soon they reappear as vengeful ghosts who seduce and brutally murder the passing samurai.

metas.name: A Tale of the Wind
metas.description:
Captures an 89-year-old filmmaker chasing the one subject that can't be framed. Ivens, making films since 1928 and asthmatic all his life, travels to China to film the wind — waiting with desert nomads, schoolchildren and a terracotta army for the invisible to move something visible. His last film; the hidden structure is weather.

An elderly, asthmatic filmmaker travels to China, hoping to film the wind.

metas.name: Sita Sings the Blues
metas.description:
Captures the Ramayana told four ways at once: 1920s blues vocals by Annette Hanshaw, shadow-puppet narrators bickering over the plot, lush vector animation, and the director's own breakup drawn in squiggles — the same story projected through four transducers, and they don't agree.

An animated version of the epic Indian tale of Ramayana set to the 1920s jazz vocals of Annette Hanshaw.

metas.name: Angel's Egg
metas.description:
Captures a girl carrying an egg she will not explain, through a drowned Gothic city, followed by a man carrying a cross-shaped weapon. Almost no dialogue; rain, fossils, water tanks full of shadow fish. Oshii lost his faith and made this instead of a sermon.

A mysterious young girl wanders a desolate, otherworldly landscape, carrying a large egg.

metas.name: Belladonna of Sadness
metas.description:
Captures a medieval witch's rise and destruction in watercolours that keep dissolving. A peasant woman bargains with the Devil across still paintings that pan, bleed and occasionally erupt into full animation and psychedelic rock. Suppressed for decades, restored now — maximalism on paper.

After being raped by an evil feudal lord and subsequently getting banished from her village, a peasant girl makes a pact with the Devil to gain magical powers and take her revenge.

metas.name: Millennium Actress
metas.description:
Captures a retired actress's memories edited as the films she starred in. Two documentary makers interview her, and each recollection deposits them inside the scene — feudal Japan, wartime, a space launch — while her one lost love stays a frame ahead. Your projection framework as a life story: the observed biography keeps re-rendering the hidden one.

A TV interviewer and his cameraman meet a former actress and travel through her memories and career.

metas.name: Inu-Oh
metas.description:
Captures a cursed, contorted Heian-era dancer and a blind biwa player inventing rock concerts in 14th-century Kyoto. Their retellings of the Tales of the Heike make the dead visible to the crowd — and to Inu-Oh himself, whose body straightens as the buried stories get heard. Music as the instrument that reveals the hidden layer; made for you.

A cursed dancer and a musician stun society with electrifying concerts in this animated rock opera.

metas.name: Rejected
metas.description:
Captures an animator's commissioned ad cartoons being rejected one by one as they — and he — visibly fall apart. It starts with a banana announcing "my spoon is too big" and ends with the paper universe collapsing, blood pooling in the margins. Oscar-nominated, quoted for a quarter century, and it still feels unstable.

In the spring of 1999, the Family Learning Channel commissioned animator Don Hertzfeldt to produce promotional segments for their network. The cartoons were completed in five weeks. The Family Learning Channel rejected all of them upon review, and they were never aired...
